chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Umar ibn Yazid said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who died and left behind his wife while she was pregnant, and she gave birth to a male child after his death. Then the male child died after falling to the ground. The woman who received him testified that he cried out and bawled when he fell to the ground, and then he died. He said: 'It is upon the Imam to accept her testimony regarding one-quarter of the male child's inheritance.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance for a newborn who dies immediately after birth in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the Shia juristic reliance on the testimony of the mother (*shahadat al-umm*) as a valid proof (*bayyinah*) for establishing the brief life of a newborn in inheritance cases. It underscores the Imam’s role in validating this specific testimony to grant the infant a quarter share of the father's estate, reflecting the principle that even momentary life triggers inheritance rights.
